verses.1: Job, listen now to me. Pay attention to all my words.
verses.2: Behold, I have opened my mouth; my tongue has spoken in earnest.
verses.3: My heart is upright in my words, and my lips speak with clear understanding.
verses.4: The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.
verses.5: If you are able, answer me, face to face, stand before me.
verses.6: I am like you, created from clay; from the same earth, we were formed.
verses.7: My intention is not to intimidate you, and my hand does not weigh heavily on you.
verses.8: I heard you speak in my ears, and your voice reached my ears.
verses.9: You say, "I am clean, without sin; I am blameless, and no wrong has come from me."
verses.10: But he has found a charge against you, and he counts you as an enemy.
verses.11: He has placed your foot in a trap, and he guards all your paths.
verses.12: How then do you say, "I am in the right," when God is greater than any human being?
verses.13: Why do you argue with him, when all his words do not answer you?
verses.14: For God speaks in one way, and in two ways he does not turn back.
verses.15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people in their sleep,
verses.16: then he reveals their ear and seals their instruction.
verses.17: To turn a person from their action and to conceal pride from a man.
verses.18: To keep a soul from the pit and to preserve life from perishing in the sword.
verses.19: And to teach a person through pain on their bed, and many of their bones will ache.
verses.20: Their appetite will reject food, and their soul will long for what it desires.
verses.21: Their flesh will decay from sight, and their bones, which were unseen, will appear.
verses.22: Their soul draws near to the pit, and their life to the realm of the dead.
verses.23: If there is a mediator, even one of a thousand, to speak on a man’s behalf,
verses.24: then he will be gracious to him and say, "Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom."
verses.25: His flesh will be renewed like a youth, and he will return to the days of his youth.
verses.26: He will pray to God, and it will be accepted by him. He will see God's face in gladness, and he will restore to a person his righteousness.
verses.27: A person will declare to others, "I have sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not fair to me."
verses.28: He will redeem his soul from descending into the pit, and his life will see the light.
verses.29: All these things God does with a person—twice or three times.
verses.30: To bring back a soul from the pit, so that it may see the light of life.
verses.31: Job, listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.
verses.32: If there are words, answer me. Speak, for I long to justify you.
verses.33: If not, you listen to me. Be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: The Hebrew "בִּשְׁתַּיִם לֹא יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה" is interpreted as "in two ways he does not turn back," reflecting the idea of divine intransigence in speech.
- v. 23: The phrase "מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ" is translated as "mediator" to capture the concept of an intercessor. The Septuagint has "angelos thanatēforos," but the Hebrew supports a more general sense.
- v. 30: The phrase "לֵאוֹר בְּאוֹר הַֽחַיִּים" is translated as "so that it may see the light of life," preserving the poetic emphasis on restoration.

[1] Job, listen now to me. Pay attention to all my words.

[2] Behold, I have opened my mouth; my tongue has spoken in earnest.

[3] My heart is upright in my words, and my lips speak with clear understanding.

[4] The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.

[5] If you are able, answer me, face to face, stand before me.

[6] I am like you, created from clay; from the same earth, we were formed.

[7] My intention is not to intimidate you, and my hand does not weigh heavily on you.

[8] I heard you speak in my ears, and your voice reached my ears.

[9] You say, "I am clean, without sin; I am blameless, and no wrong has come from me."

[10] But he has found a charge against you, and he counts you as an enemy.

[11] He has placed your foot in a trap, and he guards all your paths.

[12] How then do you say, "I am in the right," when God is greater than any human being?

[13] Why do you argue with him, when all his words do not answer you?

[14] For God speaks in one way, and in two ways he does not turn back.

[15] In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people in their sleep,

[16] then he reveals their ear and seals their instruction.

[17] To turn a person from their action and to conceal pride from a man.

[18] To keep a soul from the pit and to preserve life from perishing in the sword.

[19] And to teach a person through pain on their bed, and many of their bones will ache.

[20] Their appetite will reject food, and their soul will long for what it desires.

[21] Their flesh will decay from sight, and their bones, which were unseen, will appear.

[22] Their soul draws near to the pit, and their life to the realm of the dead.

[23] If there is a mediator, even one of a thousand, to speak on a man’s behalf,

[24] then he will be gracious to him and say, "Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom."

[25] His flesh will be renewed like a youth, and he will return to the days of his youth.

[26] He will pray to God, and it will be accepted by him. He will see God's face in gladness, and he will restore to a person his righteousness.

[27] A person will declare to others, "I have sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not fair to me."

[28] He will redeem his soul from descending into the pit, and his life will see the light.

[29] All these things God does with a person—twice or three times.

[30] To bring back a soul from the pit, so that it may see the light of life.

[31] Job, listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.

[32] If there are words, answer me. Speak, for I long to justify you.

[33] If not, you listen to me. Be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

- v. 14: The Hebrew "בִּשְׁתַּיִם לֹא יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה" is interpreted as "in two ways he does not turn back," reflecting the idea of divine intransigence in speech.
- v. 23: The phrase "מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ" is translated as "mediator" to capture the concept of an intercessor. The Septuagint has "angelos thanatēforos," but the Hebrew supports a more general sense.
- v. 30: The phrase "לֵאוֹר בְּאוֹר הַֽחַיִּים" is translated as "so that it may see the light of life," preserving the poetic emphasis on restoration.
